bounds: One client scan, one retained old cursor, one inbox replacement, and sequence values 0..3 per epoch. The first page captures its fence atomically. Each page holds one row. One retained row can fail projection.
fairness: Current pages and explicit restarts proceed under weak fairness of requests and eventual projectability. The caller finishes or abandons a scan before starting a new one.
limitations: Capacity one represents the item or byte boundary. Actual envelope and Unicode byte limits are implementation tests.
Deletion or supersession can remove a retained row between pages. A projection error is attached to the current retained row and cannot cross epochs.
One explicit replacement and restart are checked. Native client scheduling, multiple clients, persistence faults and arbitrary invalid query numbers are outside this finite projection.

assumptions: No scheduling fairness. Rejected reads cannot replace a previously accepted cursor.
No scheduling fairness. An epoch mismatch takes precedence over sequence validation.
Weak fairness of continuation requests and eventual projectability. Replacing the inbox ends the old scan.
Weak fairness of explicit restart and continuation requests with eventual projectability.
No scheduling fairness. A caller can stop after the inbox is replaced.
